proposed_canonical_merge.reason: Canvas is an additional state of the aspect control already listed by L030, not an independent parameter.
proposed_canonical_merge.required_context_text: Numeric states persist in source; canvas is a native editor setting derived from viewport ratio clamped0.5..3, omitted from source. File preview compiles in the compiler context.

near_duplicates_to_retain.reason: Diagram type is a separate user-facing shortcut control; it adds no new engine. Keep preset mapping without counting it as an engine.

Layout lab scope, Compare scope, file recipe scope and CLI scope have different value sets, capture time, defaults and persistence. Merge only with a multi-context schema that preserves every distinction.
Immediate pass, pass preview and source/native rebuild have different commit and persistence behavior.
Columns is required; rows can be none and changes grid cardinality. Both are public controls.
Pass iterations versus settled-solve maximum effort have different modes, ranges and source applicability.
CLI fit, engine aspect and DSL fit serve different stages; do not merge because the labels resemble one another.

excluded_internal_or_aliases: LayoutLab.settings legacy aliases radial→tree and compact→layered are not file engines or menu choices.
LayoutOptions trace/settle/warmStart/rebuild are invocation plumbing; user operations are inventoried instead.
fixedIds/selected/containerId/viewport are execution inputs behind public scope/holds/canvas controls, not free-form user fields.
SculptLab step defaults18, clamp1..64, has no public UI/DSL setting; describe only in contributor provenance.
Layout animation duration180ms and reduced-motion/hidden-page branches are automatic behavior, not an animation preference.
Worker/thread/cancellation/caches/trace phases are implementation details, not extra atlas controls.
General file/theme/search/clipboard/export pixel-density and check quiet flags are outside layout/routing control scope; selected export contracts are included because they retain these experiments.
